transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Hernandez, thank you for meeting with me. I have your daughter here to help us communicate. I need to talk with you about something that happened with the monitoring of your grandchild's heart rate earlier today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué pasó? What happened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: During the monitoring, the machine showed some dips in the baby's heart rate. I reviewed that tracing, and I categorized it as normal when it actually showed a pattern that required more attention. I made a mistake in how I read the monitor.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is the baby okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is doing well right now. But I want to be very clear: I made an error in the assessment. I am very sorry. This was my mistake, and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you make a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I misread the specific pattern of the decelerations. It was my responsibility to catch that, and I didn't. I apologize deeply for this. Does that make sense so far, or can I explain it differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know. My daughter, tell him.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're looking to your daughter. Does the explanation of the misread monitor make sense to both of you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We are just worried. I was so scared when the other doctor came in and said something was different.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought everything was fine. Now I am thinking, what else did you miss? I cannot sleep.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see why you'd feel that way. But looking at the facts, the second doctor caught it two hours later and the baby is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Two hours is a long time for a baby.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I am sorry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who else is going to look at the baby? I don't want only one person doing this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep monitoring.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? What is the plan now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. Do we move the baby? Do we change the medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The current monitoring is sufficient for now. We'll see how the next few hours go.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And if it happens again? What if you miss it again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be more careful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You say sorry, but I need to know the baby is safe. Is there a special test?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No special test is needed right now. We will just continue as we are.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't like this. I want to talk to the head doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can probably arrange that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure of their schedule. I'll check when I have a moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter says we should ask about the report. Will this be in the papers?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It will be in the medical record.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will the other doctors know you did this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, it's been documented.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just shaking. I can't believe this happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I can't trust the monitors now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The monitors are working; it was the interpretation that was wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just check the baby again in the morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who will check? You?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Whoever is on the shift.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know exactly who is looking at those lines.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make a note of your concern.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I need a list of what you are doing differently now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see what I can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please, I just want to know the baby is okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The baby is stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But you missed it. You missed it for two hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did. And I am truly sorry for that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if sorry is enough.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My daughter is writing things down. We want a meeting.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can try to schedule something.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check the calendar.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Now. Please tell us now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a time right this second.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts the patient and remains regulated and calm despite repeated pushback and frustration.

E.justification: The error was explicitly named in the second turn, lay language was used, comprehension was checked twice, and no false reassurance was given.

A.justification: The resident used direct apology language, took full personal responsibility, and maintained that accountability throughout the conversation.

R.justification: The resident relied on generic validation ('I understand', 'I know') without naming specific emotions or deeply engaging with emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders and vague responses ('keep an eye on things', 'see how the next few hours go') with no specific timelines or patient role.
